variables.meaning: the unknown X(x) of an eigenvalue problem X″ + λX = 0 with its boundary conditions, the factor of x in a separated solution
the eigenfunction Xₙ(x) belonging to the nth eigenvalue of the eigenvalue problem in x
the factor Tₙ(t) of t with Tₙ(0) = 1 such that Tₙ(t)Xₙ(x) solves the heat equation
the temperature u(x, t) of the wire in the heat equation u_t = k u_xx, recalled from Chapter 4
the initial temperature f(x) = u(x, 0), and later any piecewise smooth function on [a, b] to be written as an eigenfunction series
the dependent variable, an unknown function
the derivative of y, the same as dy/dx
the second derivative of y
the coefficient p(x) inside the derivative of the Sturm–Liouville equation (p(x)y′)′ − q(x)y + λr(x)y = 0, continuous and positive on [a, b] for a regular problem
the coefficient q(x) of y in the Sturm–Liouville equation, continuous and nonnegative for a regular problem
the coefficient r(x) of λy in the Sturm–Liouville equation, the weight function of the inner product, positive on [a, b]
the parameter of the Sturm–Liouville problem; the values that admit a nontrivial solution are its eigenvalues
the nth eigenvalue of a regular Sturm–Liouville problem, in the increasing sequence λ₁ < λ₂ < λ₃ < ⋯ (labelled from λ₀ when zero is an eigenvalue)
the eigenfunction yₙ(x) belonging to λₙ, unique up to a constant multiple
the constant of the Robin boundary conditions hX(0) − X′(0) = 0, hX(L) + X′(L) = 0, positive in Example 5.1.3
a second function on [a, b], paired with f in the inner product ⟨f, g⟩
the inner product ⟨f, g⟩ = ∫ₐᵇ f(x)g(x)r(x) dx of two functions with respect to the weight r
the coefficients of the eigenfunction decomposition f(x) = Σ cₙyₙ(x), cₘ = ⟨f, yₘ⟩/⟨yₘ, yₘ⟩
the transverse displacement y(x, t) of the point x of the beam at time t
the fourth partial derivative ∂⁴y/∂x⁴ of the beam's displacement
the second partial derivative ∂²y/∂t² of the displacement, its acceleration
the second partial derivative ∂²y/∂x² of the displacement, zero at a hinged or a free end
the partial derivative ∂y/∂t of the displacement, the velocity of the beam, zero at t = 0 in (5.5)
the partial derivative ∂y/∂x, the slope of the beam, zero at a clamped end
the third partial derivative ∂³y/∂x³ of the displacement, zero at a free end
the initial shape f(x) = y(x, 0) of the beam, decomposed in its sine series
the factor X(x) of the separated solution y(x, t) = X(x)T(t) of the beam equation, satisfying X⁽⁴⁾ − λX = 0
the factor T(t) of the separated solution y(x, t) = X(x)T(t) of the beam equation, satisfying T″ + λa⁴T = 0
the fourth derivative X⁽⁴⁾ of X with respect to x
the second derivative X″ of X, zero at a hinged end
the second derivative T″ of T with respect to t
the derivative T′ of T, zero at t = 0 since the beam is let go from rest
the separation constant of the beam equation, X⁽⁴⁾/X = −T″/(a⁴T) = λ, an eigenvalue of the fourth-order problem for X
the fourth root ω = ⁴√λ of the eigenvalue, introduced to avoid writing the fourth root; positive
the nth eigenvalue λₙ = n⁴π⁴ of the hinged beam
the eigenfunction Xₙ(x) = sin(nπx) of the hinged beam
the time factor Tₙ(t) = cos(n²π²a²t) with Tₙ(0) = 1, so that XₙTₙ satisfies every homogeneous condition
the coefficients of the sine series f(x) = Σ bₙ sin(nπx) of the initial shape
the displacement y(x, t) of the string at position x and time t
the second partial derivative ∂²y/∂t² of the string's displacement, its acceleration
the second partial derivative ∂²y/∂x² of the string's displacement
the partial derivative ∂y/∂t, the velocity of the string
the initial position f(x) = y(x, 0) of the string; for the forced string, f(x) = −y_p(x, 0)
the initial velocity g(x) = y_t(x, 0) of the string; for the forced string, g(x) = −∂y_p/∂t(x, 0)
the cosine coefficients of the free vibration y = Σ (Aₙ cos(nπat/L) + Bₙ sin(nπat/L)) sin(nπx/L), determined by the initial position
the sine coefficients of the free vibration, determined by the initial velocity
the angular frequency of the forcing F₀ cos(ωt); in the underground problem, the yearly frequency with ωt = 2π when t = 1 year
the particular solution y_p(x, t) = X(x) cos(ωt) of the forced wave equation (5.7) satisfying only y(0, t) = y(L, t) = 0
the solution y_c of the free problem (5.6) with f = −y_p(x, 0) and g = −∂y_p/∂t(x, 0), so that y = y_c + y_p satisfies (5.7) and (5.8)
the factor X(x) of the guess y_p = X(x) cos(ωt), and of h = X(x)e^(iωt) in the underground problem
the second derivative X″ of X with respect to x
the solution w(x, t) of the free string problem of Example 5.3.1, set to y_c
the odd 2-periodic extension F of w(x, 0) in Example 5.3.1, used in d'Alembert's formula
the temperature u(x, t) at depth x underground at time t
the partial derivative ∂u/∂t of the underground temperature
the second partial derivative ∂²u/∂x² of the underground temperature with respect to depth
the coefficient V(x) of cos(ωt) in the steady periodic form u = V(x) cos(ωt) + W(x) sin(ωt)
the coefficient W(x) of sin(ωt) in the steady periodic form u = V(x) cos(ωt) + W(x) sin(ωt)
the complex-valued function h(x, t) = X(x)e^(iωt) whose real part is u, solving h_t = kh_xx with h(0, t) = A₀e^(iωt)
the partial derivative ∂h/∂t of the complex-valued h
the second partial derivative ∂²h/∂x² of the complex-valued h
